product_guards: Require coherent typed HTML 200 observations with exactly one explicit generic meta robots tag containing the noindex token. An HTTP noindex header alone is deliberately insufficient for this literal-source path, not an invalid SEO instruction. Refuse missing, conflicting, blocked, unhealthy or ambiguous observations.

A redirected entry needs a complete coherent same-host chain and an independently observed direct noindex final page. Refuse loops, external hops, HTTPS downgrades and non-followable statuses. Re-read current flat literal routing and verify every hop and status, current file shadowing/force and absence of competing rules.

Require one literal sitemap in a known static directory, no sitemap generator, and a unique current HTML source for every final page. Re-read each literal head and compare its single generic robots directive with the observations. Refuse changed robots, scripts, templates, body/comment/attribute lookalikes, nested or inert markup, duplicate attributes, unsupported sources and incomplete budgets before PUT.

Delete only exact validated XML url nodes. Preserve page files, their robots instructions, navigation, routing, unrelated entries, extensions, comments and every byte outside the removed nodes. Preserve significant path case, slash and query. Reject malformed XML, DTD, sitemap indexes, ambiguous loc elements, unknown namespaces, oversized sources and unreadable sitemap SHA.

No generator exclusion inferred by a model and no heuristic file targeting on refusal. Individual deep and bulk paths use the same free deterministic implementation. Free-form and cached GitHub/URL previews cannot bypass evidence. Delisting decides which instruction wins, so the existing premise note still requires human review, even in auto mode.

A partially verified subset can be corrected with refused URLs named; the existing advisory warns about potential hreflang partner effects. The prior loose helper remains unchanged for other sitemap families. Target resolver candidates for a stack are not execution authorization or proof that a generated sitemap is repairable.

seo_reference.usage: Google supports noindex both in a head meta tag and an HTTP header. This implementation intentionally verifies only a literal generic head meta instruction; it does not claim header-only or Googlebot-specific coverage. Preserving noindex is a human-reviewed correction premise, not an inference of the owner's desired indexation.

independent_countercheck.description: Re-read pinned main, seed, baseline and correction branches, both closed draft unmerged PRs and their exact successful builds. Verify exactly one corrective commit affecting only sitemap.xml. Independently parse all retained XML entries without inter-entry tails and compare full output bytes against removing the three unique fixture blocks. Verify fresh and saved served XML, direct noindex HTML bodies, source robots tags, the native 302 and preview headers. Normalize only the actual owned Netlify deployment-id attribute. Re-prepare the baseline and reproduce exact deletion with models, writes, targeting and quota calls forbidden.

acceptance_inventory.after_snapshot: acceptance-after-final.json in the live temporary directory

initial_red.explanation: Multiple probes exercise the same old unchecked deletion and AI fallback, not 56 independent product bugs.

first_implementation_run.explanation: Two legacy expectations were incompatible with the guarded contract. Replace the expected unobserved generator AI fallback with an explicit refusal/no-write/no-model assertion, and enrich the positive partner-warning fixture with actual typed noindex observations. Keep its warning assertion and all unsafe-source assertions. A later bench collection import typo was fixed before the frozen final runs.

limitations: Owned static HTML and literal XML only. Generated sitemaps now refuse inferred AI generator edits in this family. Header-only noindex, Googlebot-specific directives, multiple robots tags, scripts, templates, unknown routing and ambiguous multi-file sources remain outside this guarded implementation. This narrows execution safely but is not universal advertised stack coverage.

Native previews retain the noindex header and canonical-host alias context. Their sitemap serves production-host URLs with zero sitemap crawl seeds; raw counts are 0 before and after and do not establish repair. The existing exact preview-host/header projection using actually served XML measures 3 to 0 while preserving explicit meta noindex. Fresh HTTP/source/XML checks independently prove the bounded change, not production indexing.

All three measured owned witnesses are repaired and remain crawl-visible. Refused/generated/header-only/changed-source/indexable controls are tested synthetically, not rebuilt on every remote stack. No adverse counter rises in this cycle, but hreflang partner effects remain possible and are advisory rather than an atomic multilingual repair.

Source routing, current heads and sitemap SHA are re-read; later external state or concurrent branch/server changes can still occur. This is not an atomic transaction across production sources and deployment. Parser bounds are 80000 characters, not a claim of handling every legal sitemap size or HTML syntax.

No agent deployment, customer onboarding, fresh real Claude integration, production recovery replay, receipt migration, scheduler/payment acceptance, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. SQLite retains 42 skipped tests. No all-green catalog or client-readiness certification is claimed.
next_acceptance_check: Measure removal of sitemap pages responding in error on an owned rebuilt fixture with explicit preserved controls, then remaining offered families and client onboarding.
